title: DevOps Engineer
tagline: Automate the path from a developer's commit to running software.
about: DevOps engineers build the pipelines, platforms and automation that let teams ship quickly and safely. You'll containerise apps, write infrastructure as code, run CI/CD and make deploys boring.
It's a broad role that rewards automating anything done twice and understanding how all the pieces connect.
day: Improve developer tooling and build times
Respond to deployment and infrastructure issues

phases.title: Linux & networking
phases.goal: The operating system and network every server runs on.

nodes.d: Users, permissions, processes, services and package management on a real server.
links: OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Automate repetitive work with Bash, and know when to switch to Python.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)

nodes.d: IP, DNS, TCP, HTTP, TLS, load balancers and firewalls: what you'll debug every week.
Everything in infrastructure is versioned: code, config and infrastructure definitions.
Python or Go for tooling, automation and glue code.

project.d: Rent a small VPS, harden SSH, set up a firewall, serve a site over HTTPS with NGINX and automatic certificate renewal, and document every step in a README.

phases.title: Containers & CI/CD
phases.goal: Package apps consistently and ship every change automatically.

nodes.d: Images, containers, layers, networking and volumes.
Run tests, linting and builds on every pull request.
Deploy automatically and safely, with fast rollbacks.
Reverse proxies and load balancers in front of your apps.
Keep credentials out of code and images.

project.d: Containerise a web app, add a CI pipeline with tests and image builds, and deploy automatically to a staging environment on every merge.

phases.title: Infrastructure as code & Kubernetes
phases.goal: Provision and orchestrate infrastructure from code.

nodes.d: Declare cloud infrastructure in code; plan, apply and review changes like software.
Configure many machines consistently.
Pods, deployments, services and ingress: the standard platform for running containers.
Packaging, GitOps, autoscaling and resource limits.
Learn one cloud well: compute, networking, storage and IAM.

project.d: Use Terraform to create a cloud network and a managed Kubernetes cluster, deploy an app with Helm through Argo CD, and destroy and recreate it all with one command.

phases.title: Operate & improve
phases.goal: Keep systems healthy and teams productive.

nodes.d: Metrics, dashboards and alerts on symptoms users feel.
Centralised logs and distributed traces.
Security checks built into the pipeline.
links: SLSA: supply-chain levels for software artifacts

nodes.d: Internal developer platforms: golden paths that make the right way the easy way.
Understand and reduce cloud bills.

interview: Explain what happens when you deploy a change, end to end.
Debug a broken container or a pod in CrashLoopBackOff.
Write a Dockerfile or a CI workflow live.
Design a deployment strategy with zero downtime.
